etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Attested from the 18th century. Compound of いい (ii, “good”) + 加(か)減(げん) (kagen, “amount”), with sound shift from earlier よい加(か)減(げん) (yoikagen).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Borrowed from English airmail.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From English cut.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
Borrowed from German Karte.
Doublet of カルタ (karuta, “traditional Japanese playing cards”) and カード (kādo, “card”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From English grey or gray.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From English cycle.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From English typist.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From English puncture.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From English punk.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From Dutch hoos.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From English level.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From English rebel.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From English revel.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From English rent-a-car.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From 乱(みだ)れる (midareru, “to be confused, to be disordered”). Compare みだら (midara, “obscene, indecent”) and 乱(みだ)りに (midari ni, “haphazardly, randomly”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: 略 is a daiyōji replacing 掠.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From Old Japanese. Originally a second person pronoun, as used in the Kojiki of 712 CE. Thought to have gradually changed into a first person pronoun from roughly the Kamakura and Muromachi periods. Some scholars, however, point out the lack of precedent of a second-person pronoun shifting to a first-person pronoun as an etymological discontinuity; they instead explain the first-person usage as an early corruption of 己 (onore, “I, me”), with the ancient second-person usage perhaps deriving of a different root.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Possibly the conjunctive form of the verb 能う (atau).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Appears to be a Japanese coinage of Chinese-derived components, as a compound of 参 (san, “to come, to go”, humble connotations) + 上 (jō, “up, upwards”, in reference to the relatively higher social standing of the other party to which one is going).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Compound of 問(と)い (toi, the 連(れん)用(よう)形(けい) (ren'yōkei, “stem or continuative form”) of the verb 問(と)う (tou, “to ask, to inquire”)) + 屋(や) (-ya, “store”)

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Shift from toiya above.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: 宙(ちゅう) (chū, “mid-air”) + 返(かえ)り (kaeri, 連(れん)用(よう)形(けい) (ren'yōkei, “stem or continuative form”) of the verb 返(かえ)る (kaeru)).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
From Middle Chinese 平常 (MC bjien|bjaeng dzyang). First appears in the 818 CE poetry compilation 文華秀麗集 (Bunka Shūrei Shū, literally “Collection of Beautiful Splendid Writing”).
The mixed reading with goon for the first character and kan'on for the second character suggests a shift in the reading after initial borrowing.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
日(ひ) (hi, “day”) + 頃(ころ) (koro, “(approximate) time”).
The koro changes to goro as an instance of rendaku (連濁).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Unknown. Possible shared root with 肘(ひじ) (hiji, “elbow”) and 膝(ひざ) (hiza, “knee”), related to ideas of bending.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From Old Japanese, which in turn comes from Proto-Japonic *yOnkamu. Possibly related to 弓(ゆみ) (yumi, “bow”), which appears in compounds as ゆ (yu).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Phonetic alteration from 歪(ゆが)む (yugamu) above.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From Middle Chinese 決 (MC kwet).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
/kwasei/ → /kaseː/
From Middle Chinese 火星 (MC xwaX seng, literally “fire star”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From Middle Chinese 無論 (MC mju lwonH, literally “without discussion, no argument”). Compare modern Hakka mò-lun or Cantonese mou⁴ leon⁶.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Compare 眠る (nemuru, “to sleep”), 眠り (nemuri, “sleep”), 眠い (nemui, “sleepy”), and おねむ (o-nemu, “(childish) sleepiness, sleep”), all ultimately related to Classical Japanese 寝 (nu, “to sleep”, modern 寝る (neru)).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Reduplication of 種(しゅ) (shu, “type; kind”). The shu changes to ju as an instance of rendaku (連濁).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Reduplication of 種(くさ) (kusa, “type; kind”). The kusa changes to gusa as an instance of rendaku (連濁).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Compound of 聴診(ちょうしん) (chōshin, “auscultation”) + 器(き) (-ki, “instrument, device”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Simplified from 藏 (戕 → 戊).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Related to 黒(くろ) (kuro, “black”), which see for more.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: 補 is a daiyōji replacing 輔.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: A 国字 (kokuji, “Japanese-coined character”) composed as an ideogrammic compound (會意 /会意): 身 (“body”) + 美 (“beauty”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Nominalization of 仕付け (shitsuke, literally “training”), the 連用形 (ren’yōkei, “stem or continuative form”) of verb 仕付ける (shitsukeru, “to train → discipline”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: By surface analysis, 配偶(はいぐう) (haigū) + 者(しゃ) (-sha). 配偶 derived from Chinese.
